newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money rates ease as liquidity improves.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money rates ease as liquidity improves.

text.p: Croatian money market rates eased further on Thursday amid strong offer and continued high liquidity, dealers said.
"The offer is still very, very strong," one dealer told Reuters, adding all banks had positive accounts, with overall balances totalling 704.5 million kuna.

In another indication of improved liquidity, Lombard borrowings from the central bank continued to shrink as banks repaid 20 million kuna on Thursday, bringing the total down to only 6 million kuna, compared to 86 million on Tuesday.
Against a high offer of 95 million kuna on the Zagreb money market only 24.6 million kuna of fresh deals were struck.
17.5 million were call money loans, all granted at eight percent, after varying between 8.0-8.5 percent on Wednesday.
One smaller, previously struck, two-week loan and a 6.7 million kuna one-month borrowing were granted at 13 percent.
Wednesday's overnight trade totalled 10 million kuna, which one bank used to maintain its mandatory reserves. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
